key_insight: This paper introduces error-conditioned neural solvers that learn to correct their own mistakes, rather than only producing a one-shot prediction. The key idea is to combine the speed of neural surrogates with an explicit mechanism for iterative error reduction and improved physical consistency.
problem_solved: Standard neural PDE surrogates are fast but often violate constraints and struggle to generalize beyond the training distribution. Existing hybrid approaches improve accuracy by using classical optimization on PDE residuals, but they can be expensive, unstable, and hard to scale.
method: Condition the solver on its current prediction error so the model can iteratively refine its output.
Use learned correction steps to reduce PDE residuals without relying entirely on gradient descent or Gauss-Newton optimization.
Aim for a solver that is both physically consistent and computationally efficient at inference time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners working on scientific computing, this offers a path toward faster PDE solvers that self-correct instead of requiring heavy post-processing. It could improve reliability in downstream simulation, inverse problems, and out-of-distribution settings.
visual_elements: A before/after flow showing a raw neural prediction versus error-corrected output

A speed-vs-accuracy chart highlighting the tradeoff versus classical optimizers
paper_authors: Haina Jiang, Liam Wang, Peng-Chen Chen, Min Seop Kwak, Seungryong Kim
